DESCRIPTION:

Streets Ahead Properties are delighted to bring to the market this derelict cottage circa 0.59 acres, contained in Folio CE11004.
Located circa and 6.4km from Doonbeg 6.8km from the N65. Currently the property is in need of complete refurbishment and may well qualify for the Clare County Council grants available as can be described as derelict and unoccupied for a number of years. There is some structural damage to one of the wings of the property. It is an ideal opportunity for the DIY enthusiast to make a family home or a summer residence.
The property should also qualify for all the new government grants available.
The detached house is comprised of a kitchen/living/dining, 2 bedrooms and bathroom. 

The property is located near Eircode V15 X046  *for directional purposes only*.   

Doonbeg is a quaint village with shops, restaurants, bars, primary school and GAA facilities. There is no shortage of beaches in the area including Doughmor and Whitestand. Trump International Hotel and Golf Links are also within easy reach and bring tourists and holidaymakers to the area all year round. 

Kilkee is a picturesque seaside town on the west coast of Ireland in County Clare, renowned for its dramatic cliffs, horseshoe shaped sandy beach, and clear Atlantic waters. Kilkee offers a blend of natural beauty and small-town charm, with attractions such as the striking Kilkee Cliffs and the famous natural rock pool known as Pollock Holes, where swimmers can swim safely at a low tide. With its coastal walks, water activities and welcoming atmosphere, Kilkee remains a beloved destination for both locals and tourists.

Kilrush is circa 7.5km and is a picturesque market town on the west coast of Ireland, situated on the shores of the Shannon Estuary in County Clare. Known for its rich maritime heritage, Kilrush developed as an important trading port during the 18th and 19th centuries and remains closely connected to the sea today. Visitors can enjoy the town's welcoming atmosphere, explore its historic streets, and visit the nearby Kilrush Marina, one of Ireland's largest marinas. The area also serves as a gateway to the scenic Loop Head Peninsula, renowned for its dramatic cliffs, coastal walks, and spectacular Atlantic views. With its blend of history, natural beauty, and traditional Irish charm, Kilrush is a popular destination for visitors exploring the Wild Atlantic Way.
